Irish Revenue sets two presence tests: 183 days or more in a tax year, or 280 days or more across the current and preceding tax years together.

For these presence tests, 30 days or less in the tax year does not make you resident. A tax year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Revenue also allows some new arrivals to elect tax residence, subject to its conditions.

These are residence tests, not a calculation of all tax liabilities. Check the full rules before planning a move.

Source: Irish Revenue: residence for tax purposes.
https://www.revenue.ie/en/jobs-and-pensions/tax-residence/resident-for-tax-purposes.aspx

These figures count long-term moves. They do not identify individual motives or prove that tax caused the departures.

Before comparing Cyprus properties, compare the full acquisition cost.

DLS says no transfer fee is collected when VAT is charged on the same transaction for the same property, subject to its stated conditions. Where transfer fees are charged, a 50% discount applies, with exceptions.

Have the exact property and transaction checked before budgeting.

Source: Cyprus DLS: sale and exchange.
https://portal.dls.moi.gov.cy/en/application_forms/polisi-antallagi/

Cyprus 15%. Ireland 12.5%. Is the lower tax rate automatically the better choice?

Not necessarily.

From 2026, Cyprus applies a 15% corporate income tax rate, while Ireland applies 12.5% to trading income and generally 25% to non-trading income.

But choosing a market is about more than one percentage.

Your customers, sector, operating model, location and long-term strategy can change the equation completely.

If tax were only one factor, which market would you choose: Cyprus or Ireland?

General information only. Not tax advice.

Cyprus is growing. The more interesting question is where that growth is coming from.

Real GDP increased 3.3% year-on-year in Q2 2026, with trade, information & communication, finance and construction among the sectors contributing to growth.

For investors and businesses, GDP is only the starting point. The opportunity lies in understanding where demand, capital and development are moving next.

Which sector would you watch most closely?

Source: Cyprus Statistical Service, Q2 2026.

Cyprus has access. Lebanon has entrepreneurial depth.

The interesting question is not which market is 'better'. It is where the two can complement each other.

For some Lebanese founders and investors, Cyprus can offer proximity to Lebanon while operating inside the EU business environment. For Cyprus businesses, Lebanon can still be a source of talent, networks, trading relationships and regional knowledge.

The opportunity is in building structures that make commercial sense on both sides.

If Cyprus tourism demand stays strong, where would you rather place capital?

Hospitality, residential property, retail, services, or something else?

There is no universal answer. The interesting part is identifying where demand is real, supply is constrained and the entry price still leaves room for return.

B. Retail / services

€423.1 million in tourism revenue in June 2026.

The headline is tourism. The investment question is where that spending actually flows.

Hospitality, property, retail and services all compete to capture part of that demand. The interesting opportunity is rarely the biggest sector. It is often the segment where demand is growing faster than supply or execution quality.

Source: Cyprus Statistical Service, Revenue from Tourism, June 2026.

Cyprus residential property prices continued their upward trend in Q1 2026.

The Central Bank points to strong demand, particularly from foreign buyers, higher construction costs and gradually increasing supply.

That creates a more interesting question than simply asking whether prices are rising: is the market being supported by durable demand, or are buyers starting to pay too much for the wrong locations and assets?

In property, country-level growth does not remove the need to analyse location, zoning, supply, yield and exit potential.

Source: Central Bank of Cyprus, Residential Property Price Index, Q1 2026.

#CyprusProperty #CyprusRealEstate #Investment #PropertyMarket #TheSmartySolution

Cyprus increased its standard corporate income tax rate from 12.5% to 15% from 1 January 2026.

Does that automatically make Cyprus less attractive for international business? Not necessarily. A tax rate is only one part of the equation. Structure, substance, treaty access, operating costs, regulation and the actual business model matter too.

The useful question is not whether Cyprus is simply 'low tax'. It is whether Cyprus makes commercial sense for a specific business or investment.

Source: Cyprus Tax Reform 2026; PwC Cyprus Tax Summaries. This post is general information, not tax advice.

#Cyprus #Tax #CyprusBusiness #Investment #TheSmartySolution

Cyprus grew 3.3% year-on-year in real terms in Q2 2026. But the more useful question is where the growth is coming from.

The Statistical Service points mainly to trade, information and communication, financial and insurance activities, and construction.

For investors, GDP growth is not the conclusion. It is the starting point for asking which sectors are capturing demand, capital and execution capacity.

Source: Cyprus Statistical Service, Quarterly National Accounts, Q2 2026.
